title: Controlled-Z Gates via Floquet Coupling to Two Auxiliary States in Transmon Circuits
authors: Yutao Chen, Jia-Chi Zhang, Tian-Ming Li, Yu Liu, Kai Xu, Heng Fan
abstract: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for quantum information processing. In transmon circuits, higher excited states provide additional pathways for engineering interactions within the computational subspace. Here we demonstrate controlled-Z (CZ) gates that exploit two noncomputational states, $\ket{02}$ and $\ket{20}$, through selective Floquet coupling. The nontrivial parametric modulation can activate both auxiliary transitions from $\ket{11}$ while suppressing the leading exchange between $\ket{01}$ and $\ket{10}$. Based on this approach, we develop two gate protocols: a nonadiabatic round trip through a bright auxiliary superposition and adiabatic evolution along a zero-energy dark state, both achieving average gate fidelities above $99.99\%$ in numerical simulations. Control of the modulation phase further extends the bright-state protocol to conventional and unconventional geometric CZ gates. Effective-model simulations show that unconventional control improves tolerance to residual $ZZ$ coupling and static qubit-frequency offsets relative to conventional control over the parameter ranges examined. Simulations including neighboring spectator qubits show that the original nonadiabatic bright-state and adiabatic dark-state CZ protocols retain high gate fidelities. This framework offers new routes toward the experimental realization of CZ gates and their geometric implementations.
summary: This paper details methods to implement high-fidelity Controlled-Z gates in transmon quantum circuits by exploiting coupling to two non-computational auxiliary states. The authors propose two distinct protocols—a nonadiabatic bright-state path and an adiabatic dark-state path—both achieving fidelities exceeding 99.99%. The work demonstrates that careful control over modulation phases can enhance gate robustness against common experimental imperfections.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of realizing high-fidelity Controlled-Z (CZ) gates in transmon circuits.
main_result: Two protocols—nonadiabatic bright-state evolution and adiabatic dark-state evolution—were developed, both achieving average gate fidelities above 99.99% in simulations.
method: The authors employ Floquet engineering and adiabatic passage techniques to selectively couple to auxiliary states, enabling gate operation while suppressing unwanted interactions.
model_or_system: The system is based on transmon circuits (two qubits) whose interactions are engineered using longitudinal modulation of qubit frequencies. The analysis utilizes effective Hamiltonians derived in the dispersive regime, focusing on the coupling between computational and auxiliary states.
key_observables: Gate fidelity ($ ar{F}$), leakage error ($\epsilon_{	ext{leak}}$), and residual dark-state population ($P_D(T)$).
important_parameters: Modulation amplitude ($A$), modulation frequency ($\mu$), and the ratio $\epsilon = A/\mu$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the dispersive regime approximation and the ability to precisely tune external fluxes to achieve specific resonance conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the circuit architecture, the Floquet resonance mechanism activating auxiliary transitions, and the pulse sequences for both bright-state and unconventional geometric CZ gates.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the effective Hamiltonian using Floquet theory (via Bessel functions) to developing two distinct gate protocols: the nonadiabatic bright-state cycle and the adiabatic dark-state evolution. It concludes by comparing these methods, highlighting the robustness of unconventional geometric control.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, tunable Hamiltonian engineering schemes for implementing fundamental quantum gates, which is highly relevant for experimental quantum computing architectures.
